findings: Retained radiolabel is not a life verdict. The eight C/H channels are schematic tracer experiments, not balanced reactions; abiotic fixation, sorption, isotope exchange and contamination can also retain label.
Require time-zero, reagent/no-soil, matrix, killed and recovery controls plus an orthogonal molecular/product measurement before a biological interpretation.
Outline A(e) says rare gases. Antarctic evidence concerns trace H2/CO, not noble gases. It does not establish a preferred Martian metabolism or rule out phototrophy.
Keep the original wording in the source record; use trace-gas hypothesis in the design and obtain author clarification.

Liquid water, water activity, salinity, temperature and pressure are separate constraints. A universal Martian threshold is unknown; water activity cannot simply be omitted. Incubation can alter the native state.
Log chamber/sample temperature, pressure, hydration and gas history. Validate recovery under each chosen condition and qualify negative results accordingly.

The gas/trap source proposes 1–5 sols. A 24-hour goal is shorter than one Mars sol; B 72 hours is shorter than five. The 20 Wh / 0.2 W screen does not establish heater, pumping, counting or reagent-actuation performance.
Resolve assay duration versus mission lifetime; build a time-resolved, thermally derated power and energy budget. Live arithmetic below flags the mismatch.

Raw pulse-height or photon-burst ratios do not directly equal the 3H/14C activity ratio. Beta spectra overlap; quenching, exchangeable tritium, recovery and spectral spillover can change the apparent ratio.

Calibrate single-isotope standards, mixtures, blanks and matrix effects; propagate the response-matrix uncertainty. A fraction-dependent ratio is a candidate signature, not unique proof of reductive anabolism.

C/H labels in an amine- or thiol-reactive fraction do not by themselves prove N2 or SO2 supplied its nitrogen or sulfur. -3/-2 are relevant reduced groups, not universal oxidation states for all biomass atoms.
Resolve the identity of phenylcyanate versus possible isocyanate wording; validate capture specificity and reagent compatibility. Use orthogonal elemental/isotopic attribution in ground validation.

The outline says below breakdown. Geiger-mode microcells operate above breakdown and are quenched after avalanches. The cited Failla paper addresses linearity, not an assay-specific tritium detection limit.
Specify bias/temperature compensation, photon coupling, dark noise, cross-talk, dead time, saturation, low-energy beta geometry and in-matrix efficiency.

Water and toluene are operational fractions, not perfectly exclusive chemical classes. A 100 nm filter does not prove sterile separation or analyte recovery. One gram and 0.25 cm3 are not equivalent without density. Nose penetration does not prove sampled source depth.

Measure sample mass and provenance, carryover, filter retention, extraction recovery and gas/solid/liquid label balance. Demonstrate access to the stated 2–5 cm zone independently of the penetration screen.

Parent perchlorate can be kinetically slow while irradiation products remain reactive. Neither universally reactive nor universally self-sterilizing soil follows. GEx O2 provenance remains an interpretation question.
Treat peroxide, superoxide, oxychlorine and molecular O2 as competing/overlapping targets. Validate selectivity in minerals and salts; distinguish adsorbed, trapped and newly generated O2.
410/560 nm and proposed NBT/hydroethidine/O2 indicators are candidate readouts, not unique species identifications. Matrix color, pH, metals, turbidity and cross-reactions can interfere.
Require matrix-matched blanks, recovery standards, kinetic/spectral controls and validated identification of the specific product, particularly 2-hydroxyethidium.

No measured count histories, background distribution, calibration, extraction yield, LOD/LOQ, biological replication or false-positive targets are supplied. More probes alone do not determine life-detection probability.

Predeclare endpoints and error rates; separate independent samples from repeated counts; establish detection capability using blank and low-level validation data. No assay sensitivity or life probability is computed here.
The consulted C-Series datasheet recommends operation from −40 to +85 °C. Ambient Mars or heat-shield model temperatures do not establish detector temperature or gain stability.
Provide an electronics enclosure thermal model and measured detector temperature/bias calibration; do not assume a room-temperature sensitivity applies in flight.

A reagent/device trade and laboratory outline are not a packaged, impact-qualified payload. Planetary protection, contamination controls, sealing, storage stability and post-impact calibration remain open.
Complete component mass/volume boundaries and integrated environmental, shock, contamination and sample-transfer verification before flight selection.
requirements: Capture the selected mass; identify probe, site, acquired depth, timestamp and thermal history; distinguish emplacement from sampled material.
Provide independently identified test, no-soil/reagent, matrix/killed, time-zero and recovery-control paths. Record which controls are on-board versus ground-only; do not assume all fit one probe.
Channel allocation, carryover matrix and blinded analog validation.
Separate isotope and unlabeled conditions; log valve state, pressure, temperature, inventory and leakage. Preserve label accountability without claiming a selected flight dose.
Material compatibility, sealing and traceable reference/recovery measurements.
Establish each protocol temperature/hydration/pressure state and its incubation duration. Keep the dry gas/trap workflow distinct from the wet extraction concept.
Measured thermal balance, environmental sensing and complete energy profile.
Demonstrate filtering, gas removal, carbonate discrimination and fraction recovery. Characterize reagent, membrane, adsorption and mineral backgrounds.
Recovery/cross-contamination validation; no assumed perfect solvent selectivity.
Acquire pulse-height/time/count data, bias and temperature alongside dark/blank records; retain calibrations and isotope-response matrices.
In-matrix 3H/14C efficiency, spillover and detection-limit validation.
Treat capture chemistry as a development trade pending reagent identity, specificity, target recovery and elemental-source attribution.
Orthogonal compound characterization and abiotic interference studies.
Trade peroxide/oxidant and molecular-O2 measurements as a precursor payload alternative; include spectral/kinetic and mineral-matrix controls.
Validated chemical identification and demonstrated optical/electronic resource budget.
Store raw signals, blanks, calibration versions, control identities, temperature/pressure histories, errors and censored results; no onboard life/no-life verdict.
End-to-end record recovery, relay/contact budget and reset-safe storage.
Survive delivery without invalidating the experiment
Verify that sample ports, seals, reagents, filters, detector optics and calibration remain functional after the predicted impact environment.
Integrated shock/thermal/vacuum and post-impact assay validation; peak point-mass deceleration is not instrument qualification.
